question: A developer moves an Update Set containing five new Business Rules from a dev instance to production. After the move, QA notices that the test incident records they created while developing are missing from production. Why weren't those incidents included?

choices.text: The Update Set move failed silently and needs to be retried
Update Sets capture configuration/customization changes (like Business Rules), not business data created by users (like incident records) — those were never going to move with it
Incident records are excluded from Update Sets only if they are in a Resolved or Closed state
The developer needed to manually add each incident record to the Update Set before moving it

explanation: Update Sets track configuration changes — new/modified records in tables like sys_script (Business Rules), sys_dictionary, forms, etc. — not ordinary business/transactional data such as incidents, which live outside that change-tracking mechanism entirely.
pieges: Expecting an Update Set to behave like a full data export/import that carries business records along with configuration.
Thinking test data needs to be manually curated into the Update Set — it structurally isn't the right tool for that at all.
